Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test calls MathArrays.linearCombination with arrays of length 1. The code of linearCombination expects arrays a and b of the same length, verified at lines 817-818. It creates an array prodHigh of the same length (line 823). It then calculates high and low products for each pair of elements at lines 826-842.

The problem occurs at line 846: double prodHighNext = prodHigh[1]; This unconditionally accesses index 1 of prodHigh. If the input arrays have length 1, prodHigh only has index 0, so this causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

The loop starting at line 852 iterates from 1 up to len-1 (exclusive), which will skip if len==1, but the access prodHigh[1] before the loop is unconditional and problematic.

The current implementation assumes at least length 2 arrays during the combining phase. The bug report suggests the method should handle length 1 arrays by just returning the simple product a[0]*b[0]. This fallback is currently missing, causing the exception.

Hence, the root cause is the missing guard or fallback for length 1 input arrays before accessing prodHigh[1]. Properly checking for length==1 before these lines and returning a[0]*b[0] would fix the crash.

Next, I will investigate if there is any existing handling for length 1 inputs or if the javadoc mentions assumptions about input lengths.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The core issue lies in MathArrays.linearCombination(double[], double[]) method. The method assumes the input arrays have length >= 2, since at line 846 it accesses prodHigh[1] without any length check. When a single element array is input, this causes an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

The current implementation builds an array prodHigh of length len, stores products computed precisely, and then combines these with error correction terms. But the combining logic assumes at least two elements are present.

From the Javadoc, the method aims for an accurate sum of the products but does not mention a fallback for length 1 arrays. The bug report suggests the method should handle length 1 inputs gracefully by simply returning the scalar product a[0] * b[0].

There is a related overloaded linearCombination method taking explicit double arguments (4 pairs), which computes accurately but is unrelated to the varargs or array-based version.

Thus, the root cause is the missing branch or conditional handling inside linearCombination(double[], double[]) for the case len==1, where it should return the product directly to avoid accessing prodHigh[1]. The absence of this check causes the ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on inputs of length 1.

A fix would be to add at the start of the method something like:

if (len == 1) {
    return a[0] * b[0];
}

This would avoid the out of bounds access and make the method conform to the desired behavior.
